source: Order from the 2018 Turkish word list of FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave (CC BY-SA 4.0), built from the OpenSubtitles2018 corpus (opensubtitles.org, via OPUS; Lison, Tiedemann and Kouylekov 2018), so it reflects film and TV dialogue. Forms were lowercased and merged into lemmas with the zeyrek analyser (a Python port of Zemberek-NLP), forms that fit two lemmas were split in proportion to how common each lemma is, and the result was cleaned by hand: names, fragments and obscenities removed, some words turned into phrase or compound-verb cards. Ranks are estimates, not exact corpus counts. The ranked list is scripts/turkish/wordlist.tsv (CC BY-SA 4.0); method in turkish/PROJECT.md 7.8. Glosses, examples and notes are original.

cards.note: As **a, an** it comes right before the noun, after any adjective: *güzel bir ev* (a nice house).

ex.en: What happened? Why are you crying?

cards.note: One of the few one-syllable verbs with the aorist in `-Ir`: *olur*. On its own, *Olur* also means **OK, sure**.
Written as a separate word. Its vowel follows harmony (*mı, mi, mu, mü*) and it carries the personal ending: *Hazır mısın?*
Case endings come after an n: *bunu, buna, bunda*. Plural *bunlar* (these).

ex.en: I'm a teacher, she's a student.

cards.note: Usually dropped, since the verb ending already says **I**. Irregular dative *bana* (to me); also *beni* (me), *benim* (my).
Irregular dative *sana* (to you); also *seni*, *senin* (your). Use *siz* with strangers and older people.
One word for he, she and it. Case endings come after an n: *onu, ona, onun*.
In exclamations it means **how**: *Ne güzel!* (How nice!). *Ne … ne* = neither … nor.

ex.en: Ayşe is coming with us too.

cards.note: A separate word after the word it refers to: *de* after front vowels, *da* after back vowels (*Ali de*, *Murat da*). The locative suffix *-de* is attached.

en: to do, to make (with a noun)
cards.note: Mostly a helper that turns a noun into a verb: *yardım etmek* (to help), *dans etmek* (to dance). t becomes d before a vowel: *ediyor*.

ex.en: What did you do on the weekend?

cards.note: *Yemek yapmak* = to cook.

ex.en: I'm going to tell you something.

cards.note: *Bir şey* (something) and *her şey* (everything) are written as two words.
Personal pronouns take the genitive: *benim için* (for me). After a verb in `-mAk` it means **in order to**: *öğrenmek için*.

ex.tr: Ne istersin, çay mı kahve mi?
ex.en: What would you like, tea or coffee?

cards.note: The e becomes i before `-(I)yor`: *istiyorum*.

ex.en: Is there any milk at home?

cards.note: Says that something exists or is somewhere; the opposite is *yok*. *Bir kardeşim var* = I have a sibling.
Negates sentences without a verb and takes the personal ending: *değilim, değilsin*. Verbs use the suffix `-mA` instead.
Before a noun it means **many, a lot of**, and the noun stays singular: *çok insan* (a lot of people).
One of the few one-syllable verbs with the aorist in `-Ir`: *gelir*.
Aorist in `-Ir`: *bilir*. For knowing people, use *tanımak*.
t becomes d before a vowel: *gidiyor, gider, gidecek*.
*İyi akşamlar* (good evening), *iyi geceler* (good night), *iyi günler* (have a nice day).
The e becomes ü before `-(I)yor`: *söylüyor*. The person told takes the dative: *ona söyle*.
*bura* (this place) with the locative. Also *buraya* (to here), *buradan* (from here), *burası* (this place).

ex.en: I bought bread at the bakery.

cards.note: Aorist in `-Ir`: *alır*. *Satın almak* = to buy (more formal).

ex.en: Could you pass me the salt?

cards.note: Aorist in `-Ir`: *verir*. The receiver takes the dative: *bana ver*.
Irregular: *diyor, diyecek*. *Demek ki* means **so, that means**.

ex.en: Would you like a bit more tea?

cards.note: Makes comparatives: *daha büyük* (bigger). With a negative it means **yet**: *Daha gelmedi* (He hasn't come yet).
Takes the dative: *bana bak* (look at me), *çocuğa bakmak* (to look after a child).

en: there is not, there are not
cards.note: The opposite of *var*. *Param yok* = I have no money.
Aorist in `-Ir`: *görür*.
*Ne zaman?* = When? *Hiç zamanım yok* = I have no time at all.
After the dative it means **until**: *akşama kadar*. After a noun, **as … as**: *senin kadar uzun* (as tall as you).

ex.en: My sister is a doctor, like you.

cards.note: Personal pronouns take the genitive: *benim gibi* (like me).
Dative *bize*, accusative *bizi*, genitive *bizim* (our).
*İşe gitmek* = to go to work.
The plural **you**, and the polite **you** for one person. Dative *size*, genitive *sizin* (your).
*Her şey* (everything), *her zaman* (always), *herkes* (everyone).
Also *birisi*. *İçlerinden biri* = one of them.
*Niye* is a more casual **why**. As a noun, **reason**: *Bunun nedeni ne?*

ex.en: I'm so tired that I can't sleep.

cards.note: Written apart as a conjunction. The suffix *-ki* is attached (*evdeki*), and it is fused in *belki, çünkü, sanki*.

ex.en: How do you get to school?

cards.note: *Nasılsın?* = How are you?
Takes possessive endings: *kendim, kendin, kendisi*. Before a noun it means **own**: *kendi evim* (my own house).

en: what about … (ya sen: what about you)
cards.note: *Ya da* means **or**: *çay ya da kahve*. Alone it can also mean **really?** or **oh**.
Points to something near the listener or about to be named. Case endings come after an n: *şunu, şuna*.
Aorist in `-Ir`: *kalır*. *Geç kalmak* = to be late.
*Böyle* (like this), *şöyle* (like this, as follows) and *öyle* (like that) go with *bu, şu, o*. *Öyle mi?* = Really?
What you think about takes the accusative: *seni düşünüyorum*.
After the ablative it means **after**: *dersten sonra* (after class).
Aorist in `-Ir`: *bulur*.
Also *haydi*. *Hadi gidelim* = Let's go.

ex.en: Is there a free seat here?

cards.note: *Yere düştü* = it fell on the floor. *Yerine* = instead of.

ex.en: I left the house at eight.

cards.note: The place you leave takes the ablative: *evden çıkmak*; where you climb takes the dative: *dağa çıkmak*.

ex.en: My mother works at a hospital.

cards.note: *Sınava çalışmak* = to study for an exam; `-mAyA çalışmak` = to try to.
Used in the third person: *gitmem gerekiyor* is literally **my going is necessary**.

ex.en: Have you ever been to Istanbul?

cards.note: With a negative verb: *Hiç bilmiyorum* (I have no idea at all).
*Nereye* (where to), *nereden* (where from), *nereli* (from where, of a person).
Accusative *onları*, dative *onlara*, genitive *onların* (their). With *onlar* the plural ending of the verb is often left out.
*Biriyle konuşmak* = to talk with someone.

ex.en: I think it's going to rain.

cards.note: Aorist in `-Ir`: *sanır*. *Sanırım* (I think) is very common.
Before an adjective: *en iyi* (best), *en büyük* (biggest).

ex.en: We moved to Ankara two years ago.

cards.note: After a time it means **ago**; after the ablative, **before**: *yemekten önce* (before the meal).
*Kimin* (whose), *kime* (to whom), *kimi* (whom).

ex.en: The children are playing in the garden.

cards.note: k becomes ğ before a vowel: *çocuğu, çocuğum*.
*Evde* (at home), *eve* (home, homewards).
Nouns after a number stay singular: *iki çay*, not *iki çaylar*.

ex.en: My father is a cook in a restaurant.
Your bag is over there, on the table.

cards.note: *ora* (that place) with the locative. Also *oraya* (to there), *oradan* (from there).
*Anladım* (I've got it) uses the past where English uses the present.
*Kız kardeş* = sister.

ex.en: I left my bag at the hotel.

cards.note: Aorist in `-Ir`: *bırakır*. *Sigarayı bırakmak* = to quit smoking.

ex.en: My mom is a really good cook.

cards.note: *Teşekkürler* is shorter and more casual. The reply is *rica ederim*.

ex.en: Do you have any other questions?

cards.note: After the ablative it means **apart from**: *senden başka* (apart from you).
Takes the accusative: *seni seviyorum*. With things it usually means **to like**.

ex.en: Does he always talk like this?
I waited for you at the door.

cards.note: Takes the accusative: *seni bekliyorum* (I'm waiting for you).
Both **to look for** (*Anahtarımı arıyorum*) and **to phone** (*Annemi aradım*).

ex.en: Life in Istanbul is very expensive.

cards.note: *Geçen hafta* = last week. *Geçmiş olsun!* = Get well soon.

ex.en: I'll give the book back tomorrow.
What time are you coming home?

cards.note: *Sağa dönmek* = to turn right.
Aorist in `-Ir`: *durur*. *Dur!* = Stop! Wait!

ex.en: Oh my God, we're really late!

cards.note: Capitalized when it means God. *Aman Tanrım!* is common in dubbed films; in everyday speech people also say *Allah'ım!*

ex.en: Could you close the door, please?

cards.note: *İşte bu!* = That's it!
Comes after the word it stresses.

ex.en: The key is in the bag.

cards.note: Mostly with possessive and case endings: *içinde* (inside), *içine* (into), *içinden* (out of).

ex.en: This heat is going to kill me!

cards.note: The causative of *ölmek* (to die): literally **to make die**.
*Yolda* = on the way. *İyi yolculuklar!* = Have a good trip!

ex.en: If it rains, we'll stay home.

cards.note: Optional: the conditional suffix `-sA` on the verb already says **if**.

ex.en: I couldn't come because I was sick.
OK, so what do we do now?

cards.note: With a negative, **not anymore**; with a positive, **now, from now on**: *Artık hazırım*.
*Tek başına* = on your own.
Aorist in `-Ir`: *ölür*. *Açlıktan ölmek* (to die of hunger) is the everyday **to be starving**.
After the dative it means **towards**: *eve doğru* (towards home).

ex.en: Mr Yılmaz is waiting for you.

cards.note: Formal title before a surname, mostly in writing and dubbed films; in speech people say *Ahmet Bey*. *Baylar* on a door = Men.

ex.en: I went to bed really late last night.

cards.note: *İyi geceler* = Good night.
*Yardım etmek* = to help, with the dative: *bana yardım et*.
As a noun, **end**: *filmin sonu* (the end of the movie). *Sonunda* = finally.

ex.en: What did you have for dinner?

cards.note: Irregular: *yiyor, yiyecek*. The same word is a noun, **food, meal**.
Takes the dative: *işe başlamak* (to start work).
Takes the dative: *odaya girmek* (to go into the room).

ex.en: Turkish is hard, but very beautiful.

cards.note: `-mAk` *zorunda olmak* = to have to: *gitmek zorundayım*.
*Baştan* = from the start; *tek başına* = alone.

ex.en: I'm going to the movies with my friends.
My older brother lives in Germany.

cards.note: k becomes ğ before a vowel: *büyüğü*.

ex.en: Do you have any money on you?

ex.tr: Bana bir bardak su getirir misin?
ex.en: Could you bring me a glass of water?

cards.note: Built on *gelmek*: literally **to make come**.
Used with a negative verb. *Hiçbiri* = none of them.
After the ablative it means **more than**: *bir saatten fazla* (more than an hour).

ex.en: I'm very busy at the moment.

cards.note: *Şu an* or *şu anda* = right now; *bir an* = for a moment.

ex.en: I lived in Berlin for three years.

cards.note: *Oturmak* is also used for living somewhere: *Kadıköy'de oturuyorum*.
*Arasında* = between, among; *arada bir* = now and then.

ex.en: I'm going to Turkey next year.

cards.note: *Sene* means the same.
Often attached as `-(y)lA`: *otobüsle* (by bus), *arkadaşımla* (with my friend).

ex.en: The weather is really bad today.

cards.note: `-(y)A` *ihtiyacım var* = I need … . ç becomes c before a vowel: *ihtiyacı*.

ex.en: I was late because of the traffic.

cards.note: *Bu yüzden* = that's why, so.

ex.en: Of course, I'd be glad to help.

cards.note: Also *tabii ki*. Often misspelled *tabi*.
With a negative verb: *Kimse gelmedi* (Nobody came).

ex.en: You always say the same thing.

cards.note: *Hepimiz* (all of us), *hepiniz* (all of you).
*İsim* means the same. *Adın ne?* = What's your name?
Written with circumflexes; *hala* without them is **paternal aunt**.
Before a verb it means **just**: *Yeni geldim* (I've just arrived).

ex.en: All my friends came to the wedding.

cards.note: Same as *bütün*.
*Görünüşe göre* = apparently.
*Araba kullanmak* = to drive.
*Sorun değil* = No problem. Not to be confused with *sorun!* (ask!).
Takes a singular verb: *Herkes geldi*.
Polite. Also the usual answer when someone calls your name, and on the phone.
`-DAn` *emin olmak* = to be sure of something.
Takes the dative: *bana inan* (believe me). *İnanamıyorum!* = I can't believe it!

ex.en: I asked the teacher a question.

cards.note: The person asked takes the dative: *ona sor* (ask him).

ex.en: All right, let's talk again tomorrow.

cards.note: A little more formal than *peki* or *tamam*.

ex.en: Ms Demir is in a meeting right now.

cards.note: Formal title before a surname (in speech, *Ayşe Hanım*). *Bayanlar* on a door = Women. For **woman** in general, many speakers prefer *kadın*.
*Konusunda* = about, on the subject of.
Takes the accusative: *beni dinle*, *müzik dinlemek*.

ex.en: Why are you so sad today?

cards.note: *Üzgünüm* = I'm sorry (to hear that).

ex.en: Our first class is at nine.

cards.note: *İlk kez* = for the first time.
Takes front-vowel suffixes despite its a: *saati, saatte*.

ex.en: I want to travel the world.

cards.note: As an adjective, **full, complete**: *tam gün* (full day).

ex.en: Could you take a picture of us?

cards.note: *Fotoğraf çekmek* = to take a photo; *para çekmek* = to withdraw money.

ex.en: We go to the same school.
The post office is next to the bank.

cards.note: *Yanında* = next to, with (someone); *yanıma* = to my side.
Same as *tüm*.
*Hangi takımı tutuyorsun?* = Which team do you support?

ex.en: We live in a small house.

cards.note: k becomes ğ before a vowel: *küçüğü*. *Küçük kardeşim* = my younger brother or sister.
The second vowel drops before a vowel: *izni*. *İzin vermek* = to allow; *izinli* = on leave.
From *demek*. It closes quoted words, or gives a reason: *unutmayayım diye* (so that I don't forget).
*Kendini iyi hissetmek* = to feel well. t becomes d before a vowel: *hissediyor*.
As a noun, **truth**: *Bana gerçeği söyle* (Tell me the truth).

ex.en: He's an old friend of mine.

cards.note: Warmer than *arkadaş*. *Dostum* (buddy) is frequent in dubbed films.
For people and places; for facts, use *bilmek*.

ex.en: Will you show me the photos?

cards.note: *Mesaj atmak* = to text someone.

ex.en: What do you think about this book?

cards.note: With pronouns it takes a possessive: *benim hakkımda* (about me).

en: all of them, all of it
cards.note: Case endings come after an n: *hepsini, hepsine*.

ex.en: A coffee with a little sugar, please.

cards.note: *En az* = at least; *az önce* = a moment ago.

ex.en: How many of you are there?

cards.note: Used after numbers: *üç kişi* (three people). *İnsan* is more general.
Takes the dative: *derse devam etmek* (to carry on with the lesson).
The second vowel drops before a vowel: *şekli*. *Bu şekilde* = this way.
For telling a story or explaining; a single fact is *söylemek*.

ex.en: The book is on the table.

cards.note: Like *üst*: *üzerinde* (on), *üzerine* (onto; about).
*Özür dilerim* = I'm sorry (literally **I ask for pardon**).

en: to see each other, to meet
cards.note: *Görüşürüz* = See you.

ex.en: In that case, let's go tomorrow.

cards.note: Takes front-vowel suffixes: *hâli, hâlde*. *O hâlde* = in that case; *Hâlin nasıl?* = How are you doing?
Something ends by itself: *Ders bitti*. To finish something is *bitirmek*.

ex.en: I'll be there in five minutes.

cards.note: After the dative: *bana karşı* (against me, towards me). *Karşı taraf* = the other side.
Casual. *Annene selam söyle* = Say hi to your mom.

ex.en: This is a very important meeting.

cards.note: *Önemli değil* = It doesn't matter, it's nothing.
